title: NameError resolving forward ref when non-builtin type is mapped on base class in different module

labels.name: orm - annotated declarative
labels.description: issues with the new annotations-based declarative ORM approach

body:
### Describe the bug

Given a base class that defines a column with a forward ref type defined in one module, and a subclass defined in another module, resolution of the base class forward ref annotation occurs with the subclass module globals. This is an issue if the mapped type on the base class isn't a builtin, or if the annotation name is defined in the subclass module with a different type to the name in the base class module.

### To Reproduce

Given project layout:

- `app/lib/orm.py`
- `app/lib/domain.py`
- `app/main.py`

```python
# app/lib/orm.py

"""Application ORM configuration."""
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql as pg
from sqlalchemy.orm import (
    DeclarativeBase,
    Mapped,
    declared_attr,
    mapped_column,
    registry,
)

convention = {
    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
}
"""
Templates for automated constraint name generation.
"""


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    """Base for all SQLAlchemy declarative models."""

    registry = registry(
        metadata=MetaData(naming_convention=convention),
        type_annotation_map={UUID: pg.UUID, dict: pg.JSONB},
    )

    id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(default=uuid4, primary_key=True)

    # noinspection PyMethodParameters
    @declared_attr.directive
    def __tablename__(cls) -> str:
        return cls.__name__.lower()
```

```python
# app/lib/domain.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped

from lib.orm import Base


class Author(Base):
    name: Mapped[str]
```

```python
# app/main.py
from lib.domain import Author
```

### Error

```python-traceback
NameError: Could not de-stringify annotation UUID
```

### Versions

- OS: ubuntu 20.04
- Python: 3.11.0
- SQLAlchemy: 2.0.0b2
- Database: pg (but not getting that far)
- DBAPI (eg: psycopg, cx_oracle, mysqlclient): n/a


### Additional context

MVCE available as repo [here](https://github.com/peterschutt/sqla-mvce).

I've got a quick and dirty fix in the README that works for this case that relies on traversing the MRO and pulling globals from the module of any class that has `__annotations__`, but it isn't correct.
